title: Keep the staggered buying on schedule: tranche 3 on Nov 2, tranche 4 on Nov 9
why: Nifty is still stuck near 22,700, about 14% below its January high. Brent crossed $115 after the Saudi refinery attack, and the Fed held rates with two members voting for a hike. Both are headwinds, but they're already showing in prices. Staggering protects you if it falls further.
how: Sell ~₹9,000 of LIQUIDCASE and buy NIFTYBEES (or add to Life Cycle 2041) on Mon Nov 2 and again on Mon Nov 9, after 10:00 IST. If you skipped the Oct 19 and Oct 26 tranches, split the missed ₹18,000 across these two dates. If Nifty closes below 21,800, do the remaining tranches together.

title: Profit halved. Hold, no adds, exit if it closes below ₹196
why: Q2 profit fell 51% to ₹340 cr. Income more than doubled (+132%) and Jio Credit's loan book reached ₹37,320 cr, but no dividend income, a higher tax rate and more provisions dragged profit down. The stock has slid to about ₹205, below the ₹210 level the last brief set for adding.
how: No new money. If it closes below ₹196, sell the position (about ₹4k) and move it to NIFTYBEES rather than averaging down. Look again after Q3 results in January.

title: November contribution on Mon Nov 2
why: Your monthly additions are the biggest driver of long-term wealth. Buying through a correction lowers your average cost.
how: Follow the monthly plan card: ₹10k Life Cycle 2041 SIP, ₹5k NIFTYBEES, ₹2.5k kept in LIQUIDCASE for a watchlist entry.

title: Gold is your crude-shock hedge. Hold, don't add.
why: Middle East risk and a weak rupee (~95/$) support gold, and it cushions the equity slide. It's still above its 10% target, so new money goes to equity.
how: No action. Future gold buys go into GOLDBEES only.

title: Order-win watchlist: buy pullbacks, not gap-ups
why: Railway and defence order flow continues: Jupiter Wagons won a ₹1,140 cr railway order today (+9%), IRCON ₹862 cr this month, BEL ₹730 cr. Stocks usually give back part of an order-day jump.
how: For at most one stock, wait 3–5 sessions after the news and buy no more than ₹2,500–3,000 if it pulls back 5% or more from the spike. Keep all direct stocks combined under 10% of the portfolio.

title: Don't bottom-fish airlines, paints or oil marketing companies while Brent is above $110
why: These sectors' costs rise directly with crude, and an unresolved supply shock can cut their earnings for quarters. Options and leverage remain off-limits.
how: Revisit if Brent falls back below $100. Keep every trade CNC only.
